referrals.name: Mrs Pauline Ahmed
referrals.text: Mrs Pauline Ahmed, aged 70, is being discharged from hospital following a fall at home and is being referred for end of life care. She walks with a frame and does not require a hoist. The district nurse has delegated her morning insulin injection to the agency, and carers will be trained to administer it. Carers must support her with personal care, including a strip wash and continence pads. Two calls are requested per day: one in the morning and one at bedtime. A neighbour visits at teatime most days. Mrs Ahmed is happy to have male or female carers.

referrals.name: Mrs Irene Singh

The District Nurse has delegated a morning insulin injection to the agency; carers will be trained to administer this. She requires support with personal care, including a strip wash and continence pads, and will accept women carers only for washing. She needs three calls a day for administration of her epilepsy medicine on time in the morning and to hand out tablets from her pharmacy blister pack at lunch and bedtime.

referrals.name: Mr Arjun Rahman

Mr Rahman is autistic and finds changes to his routine very hard. Carers are required to give him his insulin each morning, as he can no longer manage the pen. The Parkinson's medication is time-critical and must be given at 8am, within 30 minutes. Carers are to give his tablets from the pharmacy blister pack. Three calls a day are requested: morning, lunch and bedtime.

referrals.name: Mrs Hilda Ali
referrals.text: Referral for Mrs Hilda Ali, 91, discharged from hospital following a fall, living alone. The patient has no memory concerns. Carers are required to administer medication as prescribed and provide support with personal care, including a strip wash and continence pads. Carers must also administer insulin in the morning, as Mrs Ali can no longer manage the pen. Mrs Ali requires calls at breakfast, lunch, teatime and bedtime and has specified that only men are to assist with personal care.

referrals.name: Mrs Pauline Walsh
referrals.text: Referral for Mrs Pauline Walsh, 65, living alone. Discharged after a fall. Requires support with personal care, including a strip wash and continence pads. Needs carers to administer medication as prescribed. She lives with vascular dementia and becomes distressed by unfamiliar faces. Her Parkinson's medication is time-critical and must be given at 8am, within 30 minutes. Mrs Walsh would like male carers only for personal care. The district nurse visits each morning to give her insulin. She needs a double-up call with a ceiling hoist for transfers. Four calls a day are required: morning, lunch, teatime and bedtime.
